bottom_line: Atorvastatin 80 mg/d vs placebo initiated 24 to 96 hours after an acute coronary syndrome reduced the primary end point (RR, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.70-1.00).
implications: Within 16 weeks after acute coronary syndrome, this trial’s numbers support that atorvastatin 80 mg/d lowered the composite primary end point compared with placebo (RR, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.70-1.00; P=.048), with no significant differences reported for death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or cardiac arrest, and with a higher rate of abnormal liver transaminases (2.5% vs 0.6%).

major_points.text: Randomized, double-blind trial with 16-week follow-up at 122 centers.
major_points.quote: Design and Setting A randomized, double-blind trial conducted from May 1997 to September 1999, with follow-up through 16 weeks at 122 clinical centers

major_points.text: Adults with unstable angina or non–Q-wave acute myocardial infarction were enrolled (n=3086).
major_points.quote: Patients A total of 3086 adults aged 18 years or older with unstable angina or non– Q-wave acute myocardial infarction.

major_points.text: Study drug was initiated between 24 and 96 hours after hospital admission.
major_points.quote: between 24 and 96 hours after hospital admission.

major_points.text: Primary end point was a composite including death, MI, cardiac arrest with resuscitation, or recurrent symptomatic ischemia with objective evidence requiring emergency rehospitalization.
major_points.quote: Primary end point event defined as death, nonfatal acute myocardial infarction, cardiac arrest with resuscitation, or recurrent symptomatic myo- cardial ischemia with objective evidence and requiring emergency rehospitalization.

major_points.text: Primary end point occurred less often with atorvastatin than placebo (14.8% vs 17.4%; RR 0.84; 95% CI 0.70-1.00; P=.048).
major_points.quote: A primary end point event occurred in 228 patients (14.8%) in the atorvas- tatin group and 269 patients (17.4%) in the placebo group (relative risk [RR], 0.84; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.70-1.00; P=.048).

major_points.text: No significant differences for death, nonfatal MI, or cardiac arrest; reduction was seen for symptomatic ischemia requiring rehospitalization.
major_points.quote: There were no significant differences in risk of death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or cardiac arrest between the atorvastatin group and the placebo group, although the atorvastatin group had a lower risk of symptomatic ischemia

major_points.text: Fewer strokes were reported with atorvastatin than placebo (12 vs 24 events; P=.045).
major_points.quote: there were fewer strokes in the atorvastatin group than in the placebo group (12 vs 24 events; P=.045).

major_points.text: Abnormal liver transaminases (>3 times ULN) were more common with atorvastatin (2.5% vs 0.6%; P<.001).
major_points.quote: Abnormal liver transaminases (.3 times upper limit of normal) were more common in the atorvastatin group than in the placebo group (2.5% vs 0.6%; P,.001).
